Respondents have not raised any statutory defence nor have produced or pleaded that the offending bus was insured. As occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle owned by Respondent no.2 and driven by Respondent no.1 stands proved, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to compensate the injured/petitioner. 14. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.11.11 17:12:25 +0530 MACT NO:521/18 Fateh Ram v. Nisar P.No. 6 Of 20 BK Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. Priya vs Ajay Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135753526/ 4 15. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.11.11 17:12:35 +0530 MACT NO:521/18 Fateh Ram v. Nisar P.No. 7 Of 20 BK (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 15.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 15.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 15.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 15.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 15.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f Priya vs Ajay Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135753526/ 5 injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. Hence, compensation towards loss of f u t u r e i n c o m e i s a s s e s s e d t o R s . 8 2 7 9 / - ( m o n t h l y i n c o m e ) X 1 (month)X17(multiplier)+40% of total income(as future prospect)=Rs.1,97,040/-.
texts.facts: 1 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Ms. Priya suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 19.11.2019 at around 4.30 PM, petitioner/injured was returning from work/Shree Ram School, Greater NOIDA, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. When she reached opposite Victory One Society, a vehicle(Bus) bearing no. HR-55AD-2740(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came at high speed, driver in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner from front side. Petitioner sustained injuries all over her body and index finger was amputated in the accident. Injured was taken for treatment to Bhagwati Nursing Home, Dadri, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P from where she was referred to Guru Teg Bahadur hospital Dilshad Garden and Dr. Hegdewar Arogya Sansthan, Karkardooma, Delhi. 3. On the complaint of petitioner's son,an FIR 605/2019 was registered u/s 279,338 of IPC PS Ecotech-III, Gautam Budh CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2024.11.11 GUPTA 17:11:43 +0530 MACT NO:521/18 Fateh Ram v. Nisar P.No. 2 Of 20 BK Nagar, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver and Respondent no.2 is owner of the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle is uninsured. 5. Respondent no.1& 2 filed reply denying the occurrence of the accident or involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident. 6. Vide order dated 21.10.2021, following issues were framed. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove her claim, petitioner led her evidence by examining himself as PW-1. She testified by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. As per the affidavit, on 19.11.2019 at around 4.30 pm., the petitioner was returning from her work/Shree Ram School, Greater NOIDA, U.P. to home on foot. She reiterated the contents of the petition regarding manner of accident. Petitioner sustained right hand 2nd finger amputation and various injuries all over body. She testified as to her marital status and that she was having three kids, she claimed to be the sole bread earner of her family. She relied upon her Aadhar card and PAN Card as Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: Priya vs Ajay Kumar on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135753526/ 2 2024.11.11 17:11:52 +0530 MACT NO:521/18 Fateh Ram v. Nisar P.No. 3 Of 20 BK Ex.PW-1/1, MLC as Ex.PW-1/2, Treatment records as Ex.PW-1/3, Original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/4, FIR as Ex.PW-1/5, DL as of driver/R-1 as Ex.PW-1/7, RC as Ex.PW-1/8, site plan as Ex.PW-1/9, mechanical inspection as Ex.PW-1/10, chargesheet as Ex.PW-1/11 and disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/12. She claimed to have been earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. by working in private school and that she could not continue to work due to the accident. PW-1 was duly cross-examined by learned counsel for Respondent no.1 and 2. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 20% of this amount would be Rs.39,408/-. Petitioner has relied upon the original medical bills as Ex.PW-1/4 of Rs.1380/-, however, total of medical bills come to Rs.1367/-. (iii) Percentage of loss of earning Already granted capacity in relation to disability: (iv) Loss of future Income: The Rs.39,048/- functional disability is taken 20%. Total Compensation Rs.1,68,694/- Deduction, if any, Nil Total Compensation after deduction Rs.1,68,694/- Interest Simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of Petition till actual realization of Award amount/ compensation. 21. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.1,68,694/- with simple interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of Petition till its actual realization. As already decided, principal award amount/ compensation will be payable by Respondents with simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of petition till actual realization.
